claim.why_it_matters: Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its siblings '#### 4.2.2.1.3.2 Optional Words' and '#### 4.2.2.1.3.3 Special Purpose Words' on page 155 are headings.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page IV-8 (PDF p154) sets '4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words' as a numbered section heading on its own line, in the same heading style as 4.2.2.1.2 and 4.2.2.1.3. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 6545 it is a plain paragraph with no '#' markup, while its siblings at lines 6561 and 6565 are '#### 4.2.2.1.3.2 Optional Words' and '#### 4.2.2.1.3.3 Special Purpose Words'. The words are all present; the defect is the missing heading structure, which breaks section navigation and locator-based lookup of §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.3.1. Real as a structural (non-normative) defect. The same page's '4.2.2.1.2 System-Names' (line 6513) and '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' (line 6525) are also plain paragraphs, so the claim understates the extent.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate for 4.2.2.1.3.1, but incomplete: on page 154 the markdown also renders the headings '4.2.2.1.2 System-Names' and '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' as plain paragraphs, while the printed page shows all three as section headings and the 4.2.2.1.3.x siblings on page 155 carry '####' markup. Text is present; only the heading markup is missing.
